sections.content: How many people stayed in Histon after gaining qualifications?

Histon is a small town in the East of England. Histon does not have its own university.

Histon has lower levels of deprivation.

Overall, Histon ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 335 state-school pupils from Histon who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 165 (49%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 85 (25%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Histon to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Histon's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Histon in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Histon move to?

Of Histon's graduates, 65 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 25 of those graduates (38%) were living fairly locally, in the Cambridge travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Histon's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 30 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

Of those in Histon's GCSE cohort:

  • 40 graduates left the East of England

In 2018 to 2019, 29% of graduates living in Histon had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 140 graduates from our cohort living in Histon, compared with the 165 graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, 71% of graduates had sat their GCSEs in Histon, while 29% had moved there from elsewhere.
